name: Seattle
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Seattle: technology, aerospace and trade diligence, trade secret matters and King County litigation support.
hero_lede: Seattle is home to some of the largest technology and aerospace employers in the United States and a major Pacific trade gateway. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, using public records and coordinating Washington-licensed investigators and the client's counsel.
intro: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State and the economic centre of the Puget Sound region. The state Office of Financial Management estimated its population at about 816,600 in April 2025, the first time it passed 800,000. Amazon, Boeing and Microsoft are the region's top employers, and the area has the largest aerospace supply chain in the United States, with more than 900 aerospace companies. Technology and artificial intelligence firms, life sciences and cloud computing sit alongside a substantial international trade economy: regional trade approached 115 billion dollars in the most recent annual report, with China the leading trading partner and aircraft and parts the leading export.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Seattle because of what concentrates there: intellectual property, highly paid technical staff, venture-backed companies and cross-Pacific supply chains. An investor may need to test the founders and claims of an AI or software start-up; an employer may suspect that a departing engineer took source code or customer data; an aerospace prime or supplier may need assurance about a sub-tier vendor's ownership and export-control exposure. Washington's all-party consent rule for recording conversations and its licensing regime for private investigators shape how any local enquiry is planned.

matters.title: Technology start-up investment diligence
matters.text: Seattle's AI and software companies attract venture, strategic and private equity capital. We examine founders' and executives' business histories, litigation, prior ventures and public claims about customers and technology, so investors can test the representations in a deal before committing funds.

matters.title: Departing employee and trade secrets
matters.text: When an engineer or executive leaves for a competitor or start-up, employers may suspect taken code, designs or customer lists. We support counsel with background research on the new venture, its backers and related entities, coordinated with forensic specialists, scoped to Washington and federal trade secret law.

matters.title: Aerospace supplier and vendor checks
matters.text: The region's aerospace supply chain runs through hundreds of tiered suppliers. We review ownership, affiliated companies, litigation, regulatory actions and adverse media for suppliers and agents, including foreign links that may raise export-control or sanctions questions for the client to assess with counsel.

matters.title: Trans-Pacific trade counterparties
matters.text: Importers, exporters and freight intermediaries moving goods through Puget Sound often deal with counterparties in Asia. We research the corporate records and reputations of those counterparties in their home jurisdictions, and test whether a Seattle-area entity is a genuine operating business or a conduit.

matters.title: King County litigation support
matters.text: Commercial, employment and real estate disputes in King County Superior Court or the federal court in Seattle often turn on facts the other side has not produced. We assist counsel with witness location and background, corporate histories and asset research for enforcement.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Seattle
local_context.text: King County Superior Court is the state trial court of general jurisdiction for civil and criminal matters in Seattle, with its main courthouse downtown. Federal civil and criminal cases, including securities, trade secret and intellectual property disputes with interstate or international elements, are heard in the United States District Court for the Western District of Washington, which sits in Seattle. Federal dockets are accessible through PACER; state court access rules vary by record type.

local_context.title: Washington investigator licensing
local_context.text: Washington licenses private investigators and private investigator agencies under chapter 18.165 RCW, administered by the Department of Licensing. An individual licensee must be at least 18, submit fingerprints and be employed by, or be, a licensed agency; agency principals and certified trainers sit an examination covering Washington law, including chapter 18.165 RCW and chapter 308-17 WAC. TDSC does not hold a Washington licence and coordinates licensed Washington professionals for any fieldwork.

local_context.title: All-party consent for recording
local_context.text: Under RCW 9.73.030 it is generally unlawful in Washington to record or intercept a private conversation or communication without the consent of all participants, whether by telephone or in person. Consent is treated as given if one party announces, in a reasonably effective way, that the conversation is being recorded, and the announcement itself is recorded. Narrow exceptions cover threats, extortion and similar situations. Interviews connected to Seattle matters are planned on this basis.

local_context.title: Corporate and property records
local_context.text: Washington business entities are registered with the Secretary of State, whose public records show entity status, registered agent and governors named in annual reports, but generally not owners of limited liability companies. Real property documents in Seattle are recorded with King County, and the county assessor publishes parcel data. These records, combined with litigation and regulatory filings, are the starting point for ownership and asset research.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Seattle and works on Seattle matters from Nashville. We start by agreeing the purpose with the client and counsel, whether an investment in a technology company, a suspected trade secret loss, an aerospace or trade counterparty review, or support for King County or Western District litigation, and scope research to that purpose. Sources include Washington Secretary of State and King County records, state and federal court dockets and regulatory registers. Any fieldwork in Washington is carried out by investigators licensed under chapter 18.165 RCW and planned around the all-party consent rule for recording. Reports set out sources and confidence levels so counsel can rely on them.

faqs.q: Can interviews be recorded during a Seattle investigation?
faqs.a: Washington generally requires the consent of all parties before a private conversation is recorded, under RCW 9.73.030. Consent can be established by announcing the recording at the outset and capturing that announcement on the recording. We plan interviews with counsel so that consent is obtained or no recording is made, and we do not undertake covert recording of private conversations.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Washington licence to work in Seattle?
faqs.a: Yes, in general. Chapter 18.165 RCW requires private investigators and private investigator agencies to be licensed through the Washington State Department of Licensing, with fingerprinting and, for agency principals, an examination. TDSC does not hold a Washington licence; we coordinate licensed Washington investigators when local work is needed and handle research and analysis from Nashville.

faqs.q: How do you check a Seattle technology start-up before investment?
faqs.a: We confirm the company's registration and filings, map affiliated entities and investors, and research founders' prior ventures, litigation, regulatory history and public statements. Where the business depends on claimed customers, partnerships or intellectual property, we test those claims against independent public sources and flag gaps for the investor to raise in diligence questions.

faqs.q: Can you help when an employee leaves with confidential material?
faqs.a: We support counsel by researching the departing employee's new employer or venture, its founders, backers and related entities, and any public evidence of the client's technology or customers appearing there. Device and account forensics are handled by qualified forensic specialists. Our work is scoped to the remedies counsel is considering in state or federal court.

faqs.q: Where are business disputes connected to Seattle heard?
faqs.a: State commercial disputes are commonly filed in King County Superior Court, while cases with federal claims or diversity jurisdiction are heard in the United States District Court for the Western District of Washington in Seattle. Counsel chooses the forum; we tailor our research to that court's discovery rules and evidentiary requirements.
